findings.title: Java-style ChoiceFormat syntax injected into a react-i18next resource bundle
findings.body: Line 188 now reads `error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` This file is consumed by react-i18next, which uses double-curly-brace interpolation (`{{0}}`, see e.g. line 14 `error-username-invalid-character='{{0}}' contains invalid character.` and the `_one/_other/_zero` suffix convention used elsewhere, e.g. `resourceSharedWith_one`/`resourceSharedWith_other`). Single-brace placeholders and Java's `{N,choice,...}` syntax are not understood by i18next, so this key will render literally (e.g. '...at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.') instead of substituting the validator's parameters. This is a regression from the previous (grammatically poor but functionally correct) `value(s)` wording.

findings.title: Same i18next placeholder/ChoiceFormat regression as account-ui
findings.body: The diff changes `error-invalid-multivalued-size=Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. Like account-ui, admin-ui uses the double-curly-brace i18next convention (unchanged lines around it still use `{{...}}`-style placeholders for other validators). Switching this single key to single braces plus Java ChoiceFormat syntax means react-i18next will not interpolate the values and will show the raw '{0}', '{1}', '{2,choice,...}' text to admins editing user profile attributes with a multivalued validator.

findings.title: Italian text committed into Lithuanian translation file
findings.body: The fix for `totpStep1` replaces a correct (if HTML-laden) Lithuanian sentence with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users configuring the mobile authenticator will now see an Italian instruction instead of their own language. The diff explicitly shows this is a new change introduced by this PR (the previous Lithuanian text is removed).

findings.title: Same Italian-text regression repeated in the login theme's Lithuanian file
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1` is changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian rather than Lithuanian, duplicating the mistake also made in the account theme's messages_lt.properties. This is user-facing text shown during OTP setup for Lithuanian-locale users and should be a proper Lithuanian translation.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese characters used in a Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) resource file
findings.body: The fixed `totpStep1` value is `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 應用程式) rather than Simplified Chinese (手机, 应用程序/应用). This file is for locale zh_CN (Simplified, mainland China), so Traditional characters are inconsistent with the rest of the file (e.g. line 29 `email=电子邮件` uses Simplified forms) and will look wrong/inauthentic to Simplified-Chinese users.

findings.title: Properties files are read with the wrong character encoding (ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8)
findings.body: `verifySafeHtml()` loads both the target file and its English counterpart via `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(...))`. Per the `PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream)` javadoc, this constructor decodes the stream as ISO-8859-1 (same as `Properties.load(InputStream)`), yet the actual theme message files in this repository store non-ASCII characters directly as UTF-8 text (e.g. Korean, Thai, Arabic, Cyrillic, accented Latin letters) rather than as `\uXXXX` escapes. As a result, every non-ASCII character will be mis-decoded, producing corrupted ('mojibake') text inside the tool and in any 'Illegal HTML in key ...' diagnostic messages it prints. This is inconsistent with `Files.readString(file.toPath())` used a few lines above in `verify()`, which defaults to UTF-8.

findings.title: IOException from missing English counterpart file surfaces as an unchecked RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException
findings.body: `verifySafeHtml()` is called from `verify()` inside a try/catch that only catches `IOException` and rethrows as `MojoExecutionException`. However `verifySafeHtml()` itself swallows `IOException` and rethrows it as a plain `RuntimeException` (lines 70 and 79). If the computed `englishFile` path (derived via brittle string substitution of 'resources-community'->'resources' and the locale suffix) does not actually exist for some theme file, the Mojo will fail with an unhandled `RuntimeException` and a raw stack trace rather than the controlled `MojoExecutionException` the rest of the plugin is designed to produce, making build failures harder to diagnose for plugin users.

findings.title: No test exercises the cross-directory English-file resolution logic used in production
findings.body: All new test fixtures (illegalHtmlTag_en.properties, noHtml_de/en.properties, changedAnchor_de/en.properties) live in the same test-resources directory and only exercise the locale-suffix substitution (e.g. '_de.properties' -> '_en.properties'). None of them exercise the 'resources-community' -> 'resources' directory substitution that `verifySafeHtml()` performs via `file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community", "resources")`, which is exactly the logic used for the real theme files modified in this PR (e.g. themes/src/main/resources-community/... locating themes/src/main/resources/...). There is also no test for the case where the derived English file does not exist, which (per the other finding) throws an unchecked RuntimeException.
